title: Theme declaration
description: The interface's look, declared once. Every theme here is compiled into the binary and cooked as a loadable asset from the same entry. A theme is a whole style -- colours, metrics and fonts together -- so a theme built for a smaller or poorer display can ask for larger text and wider borders, not only different colours. Exactly one theme is marked "default": true; every other theme inherits, field by field, whatever colours/metrics/fonts it does not name itself from that one. See docs/subsystems/UI.md and docs/formats/THEME_FORMAT.md.

metrics.description: Whole-pixel measurements and repeat timing. The default theme must name every field; any other theme may name none, some, or all -- anything it does not name is inherited from the default theme.

fonts.description: Which cooked font asset serves each text role. "Default" is this theme's own fallback font, tried before a role-specific one is found empty and before the interface's built-in font. The default theme must name "Default"; any other theme may name none, some, or all of these -- anything it does not name is inherited from the default theme.

themes.description: Compiled into the binary as UiBuiltinTheme, and cooked as a loadable THEME_<NAME> asset from the same entry. Exactly one entry must carry "default": true.

name.description: Upper snake case. Becomes UiBuiltinTheme::<name> and the cooked asset key THEME_<name>.

default.description: Marks this as the theme every other theme inherits unset colours, metrics and fonts from. Exactly one theme in the declaration must set this true.

colors.description: One entry per UiColor role this theme overrides; the generator checks role names against the engine's own enum, so a role added there and forgotten here fails the build rather than drawing black. The default theme must name every role; any other theme may name none, some, or all -- anything it does not name is inherited from the default theme.
